paragraphs.text: A cash-secured put is a short put position in which the writer sets aside enough cash to buy the shares at the strike price if the put is assigned [S1]. The word *secured* refers to the cash: in a cash account the broker holds the full purchase price as collateral for the whole life of the trade [S1]. Assignment is the process by which an option writer is selected to fulfil the obligation of a contract that a holder has exercised, and the Options Clearing Corporation assigns exercise notices at random to clearing members with short positions in the same series [S2]. A naked put is the same contract as a cash-secured put, but in a margin account the broker holds only a margin requirement, a fraction of the purchase price computed under exchange and FINRA minimum rules [S6].

The account was allocated {{allocation.csp_pct|pct}} to cash-secured puts, {{allocation.leaps_pct|pct}} to LEAPS, and {{allocation.cash_pct|pct}} to cash under a {{regime.label}} regime with a VIX of {{regime.vix}} and a risk-free rate of {{regime.risk_free_rate_pct|pct}}. Of the capital set aside for the strategies, {{portfolio.capital_used|money}} was used, leaving a cash reserve of {{portfolio.cash_reserve|money}}.

LEAPS (Long-term Equity AnticiPation Securities) is the exchanges' name for listed options with more than a year until expiration, and they trade and settle exactly like shorter options [S3]. A poor man's covered call is a two-leg position: a long, deep in-the-money LEAPS call and a short, near-term, out-of-the-money call on the same stock, formally a long call diagonal spread [S5]. Every option premium can be split into intrinsic value, the amount by which the option is in the money, and extrinsic value, everything else [S4].

The good-to-own quality screen passed {{quality_screen.passed_count}} underlyings: {{quality_screen.passed_tickers|list}}. The excluded list is empty, with {{quality_screen.excluded_count}} exclusions. The trend board is a secondary signal only: the top trending tickers were skipped because they are not on the good-to-own list, as shown in the errors: {{errors|list}}.

The bottleneck board re-orders quality-gated stocks and never adds one. The highest-scoring layer is {{bottlenecks.layers[0].name}} with a score of {{bottlenecks.layers[0].score}} and a thesis state of {{bottlenecks.layers[0].thesis_state}}, followed by {{bottlenecks.layers[1].name}} at {{bottlenecks.layers[1].score}} and {{bottlenecks.layers[5].name}} at {{bottlenecks.layers[5].score}} with a state of {{bottlenecks.layers[5].thesis_state}}.

The sized positions are {{positions|count}} in total and include {{positions[0].candidate_id}}, {{positions[1].candidate_id}}, {{positions[2].candidate_id}}, {{positions[3].candidate_id}}, and {{positions[4].candidate_id}}. For {{positions[0].candidate_id}} the breakeven at expiry is {{positions[0].payoff.breakeven|money}}, the maximum loss is {{positions[0].payoff.max_loss|money}}, and the realistic loss is {{positions[0].realistic_loss|money}}. For the LEAPS positions, the maximum loss equals the capital used: {{positions[1].candidate_id}} has a maximum loss of {{positions[1].payoff.max_loss|money}}, {{positions[2].candidate_id}} has a maximum loss of {{positions[2].payoff.max_loss|money}}, and {{positions[3].candidate_id}} has a maximum loss of {{positions[3].payoff.max_loss|money}}. The candidate {{positions[4].candidate_id}} is sized as a poor man's covered call with a short call {{positions[4].pmcc_short_call_id}}, a breakeven at the short call's expiry of {{positions[4].payoff.breakeven|money}}, a maximum loss of {{positions[4].payoff.max_loss|money}}, and a realistic loss of {{positions[4].realistic_loss|money}}.

The risk picture: {{risk.checks_passed}} of {{risk.checks_total}} constraint checks passed, including margin usage at {{risk.checks[1].value|percent}} of the limit and portfolio loss at {{risk.checks[5].value|percent}}. Stress tests show a {{risk.stress[0].shock}} move with a {{risk.stress[0].iv_shock}} IV shock gives {{risk.stress[0].pnl|money}}, a {{risk.stress[1].shock}} move gives {{risk.stress[1].pnl|money}}, and a {{risk.stress[2].shock}} move gives {{risk.stress[2].pnl|money}}.
